objective: Prove, on the two-apart families with rule 60 or 102: (1) cutting any contact of a path (freezing it) leaves the far contact independent of the first ring at every lag, while the uncut path needs it at the lags where C(T - (n - 1), e) is odd; (2) in four rings closed into a cycle with two routes from one ring to the opposite one, every contact persists, the opposite ring's contacts need the first ring at the union of the two routes' lag sets, one cut removes exactly its route's set, and a cut on each route separates.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand from RECUR-PROOF-20261108-001's lemmas; finite claims checked): on the proved two-apart families, freezing any one contact of a path leaves the last contact needing the first ring at no lag while every other contact persists, a native separation across time; in four rings closed into a cycle with two routes, every contact persists, the far ring's contacts need the first ring at the two routes' binomial lag sets, one cut removes exactly its route's lags and a cut on each route separates.
title: A cut separates a path; a cycle of rings needs two
